chunks: And as for the right of your master/owner through property, it is that you obey him and do not disobey him, except in what displeases God, Exalted and Mighty, for there is no obedience to a creature in the disobedience of the Creator.

key_terms.سَائِس: Master, owner, or one who manages/owns property
key_terms.فِي مَعْصِيَةِ الْخَالِقِ: In the disobedience of the Creator

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for obeying a master or leader in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin defines the right of the 'sāis' (master/owner) as conditional obedience, establishing a hierarchy of authority where the servant obeys unless commanded to commit a sin, grounding this in the principle of 'no obedience to a creature in the disobedience of the Creator.' This concept, central to Shia jurisprudence, balances social order with individual spiritual accountability, ensuring that earthly authority does not override divine command. The narration reflects the early Islamic context where domestic and social hierarchies were regulated by ethical and theological limits.
